title: George Lewis, Albert Burbank and the song A La Ba
summary: Picou says Burbank was one of his pupils and that his brother wrote the words of A La Ba.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Did you ever have any business with George Lewis? Did you ever...?
Yes. I mean, did he...? I mean, did he...? You didn't play at the same time he did around, did you...? No. No.
What about Albert Burbank? Oh. Well, Burbank... That's another one. That's one of my boys. Yeah, I know that. Yeah, I know that. Yes. Way back, yeah. That's one of my boys.
I noticed that his name is listed as composer of A La Ba. How does he happen to hold the copyright on that? Do you know?

Who? Who do you think originally wrote A La Ba? Who was the first one to sing? My brother. He's a composer of A La Ba. Your brother. How long ago? Oh, they did some music. And... Did he just write the words or the music? Or both?
Only the words. Only the words. Only the words. Yes. Yeah, and...
